bib.title: Context-faithful Prompting for Large Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Context-faithful Prompting for Large Language Models", Wenxuan Zhou, Sheng Zhang, Hoifung Poon, Muhao Chen (USC, Microsoft Research). Findings of EMNLP 2023 (arXiv:2303.11315v2, 23 Oct 2023). I took the venue from the arXiv stamp and my own recall, not from the extracted text, so confirm it. Code and data: github.com/wzhouad/context-faithful-llm.

COVERAGE: 54,829 of 54,829 chars, 13 of 13 pages. I read the body, limitations, all tables and Appendix A. I skimmed the references for origins only. The extraction is clean text. Table column headers are garbled but I could reconstruct them (see PROBLEMS).

CLAIMS (ranked)

- claim: Opinion-based prompting plus an APE-generated instruction, with counterfactual demonstrations, cut text-davinci-003's memorization ratio on Natural Questions from 35.2% to 3.0%.
  number: MR 35.2 to 3.0 (a 32.2-point drop)
  setup: text-davinci-003 (175B). Entity-substitution counterfactual NQ, evaluated only on instances the model answers correctly closed-book. Compares zero-shot Base against few-shot (up to 16 KATE-retrieved counterfactual demos) Opin+Instr.
  quote: "reducing the memorization ratio2 of text-davinci-003 from 35.2% to 3.0% on natural questions."
  where: p.2 (intro); Table 1, p.4

- claim: Opinion framing alone beats attributed and instruction prompts at ignoring parametric memory in the zero-shot knowledge-conflict setting. Adding the instruction helps further.
  number: NQ zero-shot MR on GPT-3.5: Base 35.2, Attr 16.6, Instr 17.7, Opin 11.0, Opin+Instr 9.1. EM: 6.2, 29.6, 27.1, 24.9, 48.6.
  setup: GPT-3.5 = text-davinci-003, counterfactual NQ (MRC), zero-shot. po, the rate of returning the original answer, falls from 32.1 to 7.9.
  quote: "Opin 79.4 9.8 11.0 24.9" and "Opin + Instr 79.1 7.9 9.1 48.6" (Table 1, Zero-shot rows)
  where: Table 1, p.4

- claim: On Re-TACRED (relation extraction) the same prompts help less, and the Base MR is already lower.
  number: GPT-3.5 zero-shot MR 22.5 (Base) to 15.9 (Opin+Instr). F1 81.0 to 84.7. With counterfactual demos Opin+Instr MR is 11.6.
  setup: GPT-3.5, Re-TACRED with counterfactual relations, subset of correctly memorized instances.
  quote: "Opin + Instr 79.1 7.9 9.1 48.6 79.4 15.0 15.9 84.7"
  where: Table 1, p.4

- claim: Factual (original) demonstrations barely help or can hurt faithfulness. Counterfactual demonstrations help a lot.
  number: GPT-3.5 NQ Base MR is 35.2 zero-shot, 53.3 with original demos (worse) and 7.0 with counterfactual demos.
  setup: GPT-3.5, up to 16 demos retrieved by KATE (RoBERTa-nli+sts-b cosine similarity). Test set is counterfactual.
  quote: "Using the original (factual) instances as demonstrations, on the other hand, leads to limited effects or may even impair faithfulness in MRC."
  where: p.5; Table 1

- claim: Opinion-based prompts make the model abstain when the context lacks the answer. This is the largest gain in the paper.
  number: GPT-3.5 NoAns accuracy rises from 30.6 to 87.8 (+57.2) zero-shot and from 73.5 to 89.8 (+16.3) few-shot. Brier falls from 29.4 to 5.2 (zero-shot) and from 11.2 to 3.4 (few-shot). Opin alone gets 83.3 zero-shot NoAns. HasAns stays at 100% for all prompts.
  setup: RealTime QA relabeled with an added "I don't know" choice. 113 test instances (63 answerable, 50 unanswerable), first six weeks of 2022. Three demos drawn from 2023 questions. Choice probability is normalized across options.
  quote: "surpassing base prompts by 57.2% and 16.3% in NoAns subset accuracy, respectively."
  where: Table 3 and §4.3, p.5-6

- claim: The same abstention gains hold, but are smaller, on Llama-2-7B-chat. They come with a HasAns accuracy cost in few-shot.
  number: NoAns 14.3 to 36.7 zero-shot and 69.4 to 91.8 few-shot. Few-shot HasAns drops from 62.2... see the note below. Few-shot Opin+Instr HasAns is 43.5 against 56.5 for Base.
  setup: Llama-2-7B-chat, same RealTime QA. Per-token probability scoring worked best for Llama-2 and joint probability for GPT-3.5.
  quote: "Opin + Instr 87.8 94.4 5.2 88.7 36.7 65.8 27.4" and "Opin + Instr 89.8 95.5 3.4 43.5 91.8 64.9 26.0"
  where: Table 3, p.5
  (Few-shot Base HasAns is 56.5 and Opin+Instr is 43.5. That is the accuracy cost of abstaining more.)

- claim: Larger models update memorized answers better but still memorize more overall, because they know more answers.
  number: Filtered set sizes by model size are 121, 132, 756 and 2,773 instances.
  setup: InstructGPT 0.3B (ada), 1.3B (babbage), 6.7B (curie), 175B (davinci-003), zero-shot NQ.
  quote: "while larger LLMs are better at updating memorized answers, they still tend to have more memorization due to the larger number of memorized answers."
  where: §4.4, p.6; Fig. 2; footnote 6

- claim: On small models the opinion prompt does not improve abstention. It can worsen the Brier score.
  number: none (read from Fig. 3 only, no tabulated values)
  setup: InstructGPT 0.3B to 175B, zero-shot RealTime QA.
  quote: "Opinion-based prompts change uncertain predictions of answerable questions to I don't know, which could lead to worse results."
  where: §4.4, p.6; Fig. 3

- claim: The methods do not hurt cases where memory and context agree.
  number: NQ original contexts, GPT-3.5, zero-shot: po 92.1 (Base) vs 90.5 (Opin+Instr). EM 11.1 vs 57.2.
  setup: Filtered NQ set with original contexts and answers.
  quote: "Opin 91.3 25.2" / "Opin + Instr 90.5 57.2"
  where: Table 4, p.7

- claim: The prompt templates themselves. Opinion framing puts the context in a narrator's mouth and asks for the narrator's opinion, so memorized facts are not enough to answer.
  number: none
  setup: Name "Bob" used throughout. The authors say other names could be used. They give a cognitive motivation and no ablation.
  quote: "Bob said, “{c}” Q: {q} in Bob’s opinion? Options: {o} A:"
  where: §3.1, p.3

- claim: Case study. Base, Attr and Instr return the memorized Lady Gaga for the Super Bowl LI halftime show when the context was edited to say "Bosco". Opin and Opin+Instr return Bosco. On an irrelevant retrieved document, Opin variants say "I don't know" while Base, Attr and Instr guess.
  number: none
  setup: text-davinci-003, two hand-picked examples.
  quote: "Opin Bosco ✓ I don’t know ✓"
  where: Table 5, p.7

LIMITS
- Authors assume the supplied context is reliable. They do not handle retrieved contexts that are erroneous or conflicting. They write that "Assessing the factuality of the context solely based on the provided information becomes challenging". (Limitations, p.8)
- They test updated-answer extraction only. Multi-hop reasoning with the updated knowledge is not tested.
- English only, three datasets (NQ, Re-TACRED, RealTime QA), models are text-davinci-003 and Llama-2-7B-chat plus InstructGPT sizes. Future work lists open-domain QA and summarization.
- The abstention test set is tiny (113 instances, 50 unanswerable).
- Counterfactual datasets are synthetic: random same-type entity swaps.
- The opinion prompt gains are smaller or inconsistent on Llama-2-7B (opinion is second best on only 9 of 24 metrics) and give no abstention gain on small InstructGPT models.
- Cost of abstaining on Llama-2: few-shot HasAns falls to 43.5 from 56.5.
- The narrator framing is motivated by intuition only. There is no ablation of the "Bob" name or of other narrator wording.
- Dated: text-davinci-003 is retired and Llama-2-7B-chat is old. Nothing was tested on current instruction-tuned or reasoning models. Whether the effect persists is not shown.

BUILDS ON
- Longpre et al. 2021: entity-substitution counterfactuals, the po/ps/MR metrics.
- Neeman et al. 2022 and Li et al. 2022: counterfactual and answerability-augmented finetuning (this paper moves it into prompting).
- Zhou et al. 2022: APE, automatic prompt engineer, used to generate the instruction.
- Liu et al. 2022: KATE, retrieval of demonstrations.
- Kasai et al. 2022: RealTime QA.
- Gupta et al. 2019 and Bjerva et al. 2020: opinion-based QA (SubjQA).
- Rajpurkar et al. 2018 (SQuAD 2.0): abstention.
- Stoica et al. 2021: Re-TACRED.
- Kwiatkowski et al. 2019: NQ.
- Brown et al. 2020: few-shot prompting.
- Touvron et al. 2023: Llama 2.

CODE (verbatim templates, §3.1, p.3)
- Base: `{c} Q: {q}? Options: {o} A:`
- Opinion: `Bob said, “{c}” Q: {q} in Bob’s opinion? Options: {o} A:`
- Attributed: `{c} Q: {q} based on the given text? Options:{o} A:`
- Instruction: `Instruction: {Instruction} {c} Q: {q}? Options: {o} A:`
- APE top instructions (Appendix A): NQ "read the given information and answer the corresponding question." RealTime QA "answer a question based on the provided input-output pairs." Re-TACRED "identify the relationship between two entities from a list of options."

FIGURES
- Fig. 1, p.1: two examples, knowledge conflict (Twitter CEO, model says Jack Dorsey) and abstention (Bill Gates born in Seattle, asked whether he founded Microsoft, model says "yes"). Shows both failure modes in two lines.
- Fig. 2, p.8: MR against model size (0.3B to 175B), filtered and full eval sets, five prompts. Shows MR falling with size on the filtered set while the full-set MR rises.
- Fig. 3, p.8: Brier score against model size on RealTime QA.
- Table 5, p.7: before/after prompt and output comparison, the best single illustration for the note.

PROBLEMS
- Table headers are garbled in the extraction ("MRC REps"). Reading from the numbers: in Tables 1 and 2 the first four columns are MRC (ps, po, MR, EM) and the last four are RE (ps, po, MR, F1). In Table 3, GPT-3.5 gives NoAns, All, Brier and Llama-2 gives HasAns, NoAns, All, Brier.
- Text-versus-table mismatch: the text says the Llama-2 RE MR reduction is 57.3%. The table gives a Base of 81.6 and Opin+Instr counter-demo of 15.5, which is a drop of 66.1. Treat 57.3 as unreconciled and cite table values. The other quoted reductions (32.2, 39.4, 10.9, 57.2, 16.3, 22.4, 24.2) match the table.
- My first Llama-2 abstention claim above has a messy "number" field. Use the Table 3 quotes.
- The page numbers are my mapping from the text order and the table positions, so they are approximate.
- No embedded instructions found in the PDF.
- Target note 03-core-techniques.md: the grep found no existing mention of Zhou 2023 context-faithful, opinion-based prompts or counterfactual demos. The only Zhou hit is the least-to-most paper (Zhou et al., ICLR 2023). That is a different paper, so take care not to confuse the two.
